name: Cross-Border Commuter Permit (G Permit)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires living anywhere in the EU/EFTA and working anywhere in Switzerland (no border-zone restriction remains for EU/EFTA nationals) — registration-based, no quota, no labour-market test. The holder must return to their main foreign residence at least weekly.

This requires a permanent right of residence in a neighbouring country, at least 6 months' prior residence within the defined border zone, and satisfaction of the labour-market test and applicable quota.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract and evidence of qualifying foreign residence

outcome.duration_length: EU/EFTA: 5 years if the contract is 12+ months or unlimited, otherwise contract term. Third-country: limited to the issuing canton's border zone, usually 1 year.
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: must NOT reside in Switzerland — this permit does not confer a right to live in the country, only to work there while residing abroad

sources.title: Cross-border commuter permit G - State Secretariat for Migration

notes: GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE STRUCTURE with no direct equivalent elsewhere in this entire multi-country dataset: this permit explicitly does NOT confer a right to RESIDE in Switzerland — the holder works in Switzerland while living abroad, taxed via withholding at source with Swiss AHV contributions, and must return to their main foreign residence at least weekly (EU/EFTA group). This is the only route in this dataset (across all 15 countries built so far) structured explicitly around the applicant NEVER establishing Swiss residence at all — deliberately terminal in every direction (leads_to_pr: false, no family_can_join, no switchable_to targets), since its entire premise is the opposite of settlement. If a G-permit holder DOES eventually move their residence into Switzerland, a standard B/L route applies instead — not modeled as a formal switchable_to link here since it represents abandoning this route's defining characteristic rather than a natural progression from it. EU/EFTA cross-border commuters can now live ANYWHERE in the EU/EFTA and work anywhere in Switzerland — the old border-zone restriction has been fully removed for this group specifically, though it remains in force for the third-country group.
